figure.title: Five slices and what blocks them

s1.name: S1 Import instrument A export
s1.subtitle: Check: raw wells show
s1.description: Slice 1. An instrument A export is imported and every well shows its raw value. Nothing blocks it, so it starts first. The check imports a fixture export, counts the wells shown and confirms a plate the instrument flagged as failed QC is skipped.

s2.name: S2 Import instrument B export
s2.subtitle: Check: same well table
s2.description: Slice 2. An instrument B export, with its own column layout, is imported. It waits for slice 1. The check compares its well table with the equivalent instrument A fixture.

s3.name: S3 Normalise to % of control
s3.subtitle: Check: worked plate
s3.description: Slice 3. Each well is shown as a percentage of its plate's control wells. It waits for slice 1 only, so it can run beside slice 2. The check uses a plate with known control wells.

s4.name: S4 Compare with the reference run
s4.subtitle: Check: overlay values
s4.description: Slice 4. A run is overlaid on the reference run for its protocol version. It waits for slices 2 and 3. The check overlays two fixture runs, reads the differences and refuses a reference run from a different protocol version.

s5.name: S5 Flag wells outside tolerance
s5.subtitle: Check: the exact limit
s5.description: Slice 5. Wells outside tolerance are flagged. It waits for slice 4. The check includes a well exactly at the limit, which must not flag.
